output.headline: Accepts $280,000 from Alameda County for nutrition education and obesity prevention programs

money.evidence: for the latter to provide $280,000.00 in funding

output.summary: The Alameda County Health Care Services Agency will give the district $280,000 to support nutrition education and obesity prevention programs run by the Community Schools and Student Services Department. This amends an existing master contract with community-based organizations (Master Contract 900322). The funding covers October 1, 2022 through September 30, 2023.

vendor.name: Alameda County Health Care Services Agency

output.headline: Adds $558,729.45 to keep Microsoft software licenses from Softchoice through October 2025

money.evidence: for a total new three-year cumulative cost not to exceed $558,729.45

output.summary: This amendment extends the district's Microsoft software licensing agreement with Softchoice, Inc. for three more years, from October 2022 to October 2025, at up to $186,243.15 per year. The most the district can spend under the agreement rises from $466,138.35 to $1,024,867.80. The software is used districtwide.

output.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $112,000 for Climate Corps fellows on sustainability projects

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $112,000.00

output.summary: The district will pay Bay Area Community Resources up to $112,000 to place Climate Corps AmeriCorps Fellows in the district. Fellows work on projects to cut greenhouse gas emissions, energy, water and waste, and they also teach students and help with community outreach. The agreement runs September 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $90,000 for Saving Shorty staff to provide a positive presence on campuses

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $90,000.00

output.summary: Saving Shorty will provide staff on campuses the district chooses to be present during passing periods and breaks. The goal is to help students and staff feel safe and to support calm transitions between classes. The agreement began August 8, 2022, before this board approval, and runs through December 31, 2022.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $93,600 for a contractor to run arts enrichment and Saturday camps for elementary students

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $93,600.00

output.summary: The district is approving a contract with an individual consultant who works with the Expanded Learning Office on an arts enrichment initiative (theater, culinary and music) for all 51 elementary schools. The consultant also schedules Saturday camps serving 100 or more students per event and manages a professional development platform for the office. Work began September 1, 2022, before this approval, and runs through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $67,980 for Hatchuel Tabernik & Associates to plan after-school grant applications

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $67,980.00

output.summary: Hatchuel Tabernik & Associates will help the district plan its applications for 21st Century Community Learning Centers (21st CCLC) and ASSETS grants, which fund after-school programs. The agreement began September 2, 2022, before this approval, and runs through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $19,000 for HERO to lead organized recess games at East Oakland Pride Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $19,000.00

output.summary: HERO will run organized recess games and physical activity sessions and give extra support at recess at East Oakland Pride Elementary School. The agreement began September 8, 2022, before this approval, and runs through November 30, 2022.

output.headline: Adds $160,500 to Springboard Collaborative's after-school literacy program at three elementary schools
output.summary: This is the fourth amendment to the district's contract with Springboard Collaborative for an eight-week after-school small-group reading program for fifty students at each of three schools. It includes family engagement, incentives and staff training. It adds $160,500, raising the contract limit from $1,564,540 to $1,725,040, and runs through February 20, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $37,500 for Be the Change Consulting to facilitate the George Floyd Resolution Team

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $37,500.00

output.summary: Be the Change Consulting will facilitate monthly meetings of the George Floyd Resolution Team, including preparing agendas, tools and supporting materials. The agreement began August 1, 2022, before this approval, and runs through December 30, 2022.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $89,000 for a consultant to manage the rollout of Frontline HR software

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $89,000.00

output.summary: The district is approving a contract with an individual consultant for up to 1,000 hours of project management on the Frontline Implementation Project for the Talent Division. The work includes coordinating planning sessions, writing communications and training materials, and supporting employees and supervisors after rollout. Work began July 5, 2022, before this approval, and runs through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $22,000 for a contractor to coach teachers through teaching credential assessments

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $22,000.00

output.summary: The district is approving a contract with an individual coach who will lead overview sessions and give individual coaching to small groups of teachers preparing for the edTPA and CalTPA teacher performance assessments. The coach also tracks progress and meets monthly with the New Teacher Support & Development team. Work began July 1, 2022, before this approval, and runs through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $30,000 for GIBCO Environmental Service to clean up and sample school sites

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00

output.summary: GIBCO Environmental Service will provide environmental services to reduce risk at school sites, including environmental clean-up and collecting environmental samples. The agreement began July 1, 2022, before this approval, and runs through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Accepts $227,000 from First Five of Alameda County for kindergarten readiness and Summer Pre-K
output.summary: First Five of Alameda County is giving the district a $227,000 grant to support Summer Pre-K programs and to train early childhood and K-12 teachers on the Summer Pre-K model. The money also pays for a Kindergarten Readiness Director to build year-round school readiness and transition programming for families and children. The grant covers July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023.

output.headline: Pays Crisis Prevention Institute up to $234,000 for nonviolent crisis response training, without bidding

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $234,000.00

output.summary: The district is hiring the Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI) for 500 verbal intervention licenses, five on-site Nonviolent Crisis Response training sessions of up to 40 people each, and training for eight district staff to become trainers. The district is skipping public bidding under a sole-source exception, which is approved by Resolution No. 2223-0007. The agreement runs October 6, 2022 through December 31, 2023.

output.headline: Finds use of the former Parker School site for adult and career education exempt from CEQA review
output.summary: Resolution No. 2223-0031 finds that using the former Parker School facilities for Oakland Adult and Career Education is exempt from review under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). It also directs the Superintendent or her designee to prepare and file a Notice of Exemption.

output.headline: Ratifies the Board President's appointment of a member to the Audit Committee through January 2024
output.summary: The Board is ratifying the Board President's appointment of Jeffrey Hall, in his first term, to the Audit Committee. The appointment takes effect October 7, 2022 and fills an unexpired term ending January 31, 2024.

output.headline: Approves out-of-state trip to Austin, Texas for two Oakland High students and two adults at no cost
output.summary: Under Resolution No. 2223-0009, two Oakland High School 12th-grade students and two adults may travel to the Grantmakers for Education Conference in Austin, Texas. The trip is October 18 through October 20, 2022, at no cost to the district.
